blind.description: A thick, vertical rectangular stone door leaf or slab. The front face is carved with a stylized, angry monolithic face featuring a prominent brow, hollow/blank eyes, a broad nose, and a large agape rectangular mouth cavity. The back side resembles laid ashlar stonework/blocks. The material is stylized pale grey-green stone with painted green moss or lichen running through the cracks and bevels. Surfaces are solid, manifold, and continuous.
blind.from_above: A rounded thick rectangular stone top with green mossy grooves running across it, with the brow and nose profile protruding on the front face.
blind.height_vs_figure: Roughly 1.1 to 1.2 times as tall as the 5 ft 9 in figure (around 6.5 to 7 ft tall) and about 3.5 ft wide.

notes: slab is thicker than catalog footprint specification but reads cleanly at table distance
